title: UPDATE: Samsung, SK Hynix Combined Quarterly Profits Forecast at 184 Trillion Won

tickers.name: SK hynix Inc. American Depositary Shares

summary:
The South Korean chipmakers are expected to report combined operating profits for the quarter that are double what the two firms earned across all of last year. Samsung and SK Hynix share prices have fallen approximately 30% over the past month, as investors weigh these record profit projections against fears of an eventual crash in memory chip prices.

SK Hynix will report earnings on Oct. 28, followed by Samsung on Oct. 29. Current sector data indicates that high-bandwidth memory (HBM) average selling prices are projected to rise 121% next year and current supply for that period is already sold out. This volatility follows warnings from Dell CEO Michael Dell that memory shortages could persist for years and a statement from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that a memory glut is unlikely by 2029.

selectedTweets.text:
Samsung and SK Hynix are about to report over 184 TRILLION won in combined operating profit for a single quarter.

That is DOUBLE what the two companies made in all of last year.

Yet both stocks have fallen about 30% in the past month.

SK Hynix reports on the 28th and Samsung on the 29th, and 11 million Korean retail shareholders are waiting for answers.

The market wants three things: HBM4 supply updates, HBM4E readiness, and how much of production is locked into long term contracts.

HBM average selling prices are expected to jump 121% next year, and next year's supply is reportedly already SOLD OUT.

Record profits and falling stocks rarely last together for long.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Jensen Huang just pushed back HARD on the memory oversupply fears.

Speaking to CNBC at GTC Berlin, the $NVDA CEO said he does not see a surplus of memory by 2029, even after the selloff in memory stocks this past week.

"One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it," he said.

He added that HBM will be used for years to come, and pointed out that Nvidia was the first company to bring LPDDR into the data center.

The selloff started after a Korean newspaper column predicted a memory price war by 2029, and it dragged down $MU, Samsung and SK Hynix.

When the biggest buyer of AI memory on the planet tells you demand keeps growing, I would take that more seriously than an opinion column.

selectedTweets.text:
MICHAEL DELL REVEALS HOW HIS COMPANY COULD SURVIVE AN AI BUST

Dell Technologies ($DELL ) is positioning itself to withstand a potential AI downturn through just-in-time manufacturing and a negative cash conversion cycle.

Unlike heavily indebted AI infrastructure providers, Dell largely builds servers against customer orders, limiting inventory exposure.

•  AI server backlog: $95 billion
•  AI customers: 6,500+
•  Projected fiscal-year revenue growth: 70%

However, Michael Dell warns that memory chip shortages could worsen next year.

The key takeaway: Dell's customer-funded operating model may offer protection against an AI spending slowdown, although weaker demand could quickly hit revenue.

$GOOGL is now discussing deals to extend their memory LTAs through 2035 from KeyBanc channel checks. 

Samsung already has 70% of their capacity allocated through 2031, and this move would suggest a more durable cycle for $MU, $SKHY, and the others. 

They also expect HBM prices up 80% to 100% in the Q1 2027. 

Having all your capacity potentially allocated out into 2035 via LTAs would ease a lot of memory durability fears.

selectedTweets.text:
$NVDA Jensen Huang: Surplus of memory supply is unlikely by 2029. 

The CNBC question referenced a Korean newspaper opinion on $KOSPI / Samsung / SK Hynix that predicted "new supply will leave the memory sector a red ocean in 2029."

"One of the things that's really great about memory is that you can always use more of it", Jensen said, citing LPDDR usage in DCs.  And responded "I don't think so" in terms of possibilities of oversupply in 2029. 

Just my personal opinion, Nvidia probably has the most visibility in the entire industry. 

Especially around supply procurement and emerging capacity, given they're the ones leading all the architectural shifts. 

On durability, you have Samsung already allocated majority of capacity into 2031 from SED and hyperscalers like $GOOGL are already reportedly securing memory LTAs into 2035 from KeyBanc. 

Yet there's endless "it's all over" sentiment on memory now. I'd probably trust Jensen's opinion here.
